articleTitle: Casimir Forces leading to 3D self-assembled paired metallic microshutters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: 3D self-assembly of metallic microshutters into paired ones (Yin Yang shaped) is presented by combining the technologies of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) and Casimir forces using different building materials, e.g., Al & Zr. Casimir forces in Zirconium (Zr) MEMS is reported first time.

articleTitle: Non-Resonant and Resonant 2D Quasi-Static PZT MEMS Scanners for LiDAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of four high-performing two-dimensional quasi-static MEMS laser scanners, employing both non-resonant and resonant PZT actuation mechanisms with mechanical coupling. The simulations demonstrate the achievement of optical scanning angles of up to 63.76 degrees for the non-resonant mode and 231.96 degrees for the resonant mode. Additionally, the optical scanning bandwidth-efficiency product (θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">opt</inf>. D. f) is calculated as 66.68 deg.mme.Hz for the non-resonant mode and 5741.24 deg.mme.Hz for the resonant mode, establishing these devices as the highest-performing 2D MEMS scanners reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Transversal plasmon resonance observed in tapered silicon nanowires
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: It has been recently demonstrated in literature that silicon nanowires (Si-NWs) with a cylindrical shape sustain longitudinal and transversal plasmon resonances. In this work, we present the results about the electron energy loss spectroscopy on Si-NWs with tapered morphology. The Si-NWs present a length of about 300 nm and a diameter, at the base, of around 15 nm, while at the center, of approximately 12 nm. Despite the different geometry, the results confirm the presence of transversal plasmonic resonance, as in the previous study. However, the presence of a continuous signal extending all along the Si-NWs length, and for several energies, is observed here for the first time.

articleTitle: Nanostructured blazed gratings for broadband high efficiency spectro-imagers by topology optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Sub-wavelength blazed gratings designed using topology optimization are presented. They diffract light on a particular order with a very high diffraction efficiency, on a broad wavelength range in the visible and near-infrared light. They are moreover faced with preliminary results of manufacturing of metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Low Crosstalk Electrothermal Micromirrors for High-speed Resonant Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Electrothermal micromirrors face challenges of irregular scanning patterns when operated near resonance, primarily due to significant mechanical crosstalk. This paper presents an innovative decoupled electrothermal micromirror, effectively minimizing cross-axis crosstalk by approximately 30 to 50 times at the resonant frequency via an eigenmode separation method.

articleTitle: 2D Actuatable Micromirror Arrays for Smart Windows: Elimination of Stress Induced Cracks in Metallic MEMS Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Design improvements of 2D actuatable MEMSmicromirror are reported eliminating crack formation due to stress concentration. Concept and design of micromirror arrays, as well as technological fabrication and experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Atomistic Modeling of Sb/h-hBN heterostructure for potential optoelectronic applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This work investigates the electronic and optical behavior of a heterostructure composed of Antimonene (Sb) and hexagonal Boron Nitride (h-BN) monolayers, employing the projected augmented wave (PAW) method within the framework of density functional theory (DFT). We calculate the structure’s formation energy to ascertain its thermodynamic stability, considering the Van der Waals forces driving the interlayer interactions. The heterostructure formation reveals a notable band transition (from indirect to direct) compared to the pristine antimonene sheet. At the same time, there is a significant enhancement in absorption peak intensities and strong bathochromic shifting in the peak positions. The exceptional optical properties observed in the proposed heterostructure render it promising for next-generation optical applications, including light emission, detection, modulation, and manipulation functions.

articleTitle: A 3D-Printed Magnetic Focus Actuator for Laser Scanning Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report the design, manufacturing, and characterization results of a magnetic focus actuator and integrated circuit driver for use with miniaturized laser scanning capsule endoscopy. The capsule structure comprises: (1) a magnet-attached, SLA-printed focus actuator, (2) a lens and its housing, (3) a laser diode inserted into the electro coil, and (4) an actuator driver IC, which provides alternating current output at 32 Hz by down-converting the crystal frequency multiple times to match the mechanical resonance of the actuator itself. Due to the restricted power provided by the battery within the capsule, the IC is designed to mitigate higher harmonics for improved energy efficiency. Focus actuation tests were conducted following the assembly of the actuator and IC within the capsule, showcasing a total focal shift of 3.22 mm due to the interaction between the electro coil and Nd magnets.

articleTitle: Erbium-doped zinc-sodium phosphate glasses as high-gain material for integrated photonics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this paper, we characterize erbium-doped sodium-zinc phosphate glasses’ transmission loss and on-off gain coefficients. Results reveal that this material shows a transmission loss coefficient of 1.8 dB/mm and an on-off gain of 1.9 dB/mm for a 5 mm width sample, achieving net optical gain.

articleTitle: Silicon Nitride Microring Resonator with Slot Waveguide and Metamaterial Side Cladding for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This manuscript proposes a microring resonator based on a silicon nitride slot waveguide surrounded by a metamaterial cladding. A device with improved sensitivity is achieved by including such metamaterial cladding to the slot waveguide microring resonator. With that, the contact surface increases, and the electric-field enhancement occurs at the slots located at the waveguide and metamaterial cladding. The device was modeled to operate under the fundamental quasitransversal electric mode. The simulation predicts a sensitivity of about 400 nm/RIU and a free spectral range of 27 nm.

articleTitle: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy for Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: To detect early-stage Alzheimer's disease, cerebrospinal fluid samples were analyzed using the inexpensive and fast method of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy with commercially available gold nanoparticle substrates. Using machine learning, biomarkers were identified that were consistent with previous studies, with a result of 100% accuracy in classifying Alzheimer's patients and 85% for the healthy control group.

articleTitle: MEMS as Ultrafast X-ray Optics for Manipulating X-ray Pulses with Picosecond Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Our research unveiled a novel application of torsional MEMS, showcasing their ability to manipulate hard X-ray pulses effectively. This manipulation occurs on a time scale from 300 ps down to an astonishing 50 ps, a range comparable to or even shorter than the pulse length of X-rays from synchrotron sources. This ultra-fast X-ray modulation is achieved by timing nonlinear micro-mechanical resonators with a synchrotron storage ring to diffract X-ray pulses through the narrow Bragg peak of the single-crystalline material. We have achieved an unprecedentedly fast maximum angular velocity exceeding 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> degrees/s while maintaining the maximum linear velocity well below sonic speed and material break-down limit. Furthermore, we have demonstrated the potential of highly ultrafast X-ray optics-on-a-chip based on MEMS. These optics can modulate hard X-ray pulses exceeding 350 MHz, a frequency 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> times higher than any other mechanical modulator, with a pulse purity >10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> without compromising the spectral brilliance.

articleTitle: Plasmonic nanoantennas for biosensing and monitoring of cell activity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel device that utilizes plasmonic nanoantennas, which has promising capabilities in biomolecular sensing and monitoring of electrophysiological activity in living systems. The biosensing capability was validated with sucrose solutions, achieving a sensitivity of 469 nm/RIU (refractive index units). Additionally, electrical monitoring was demonstrated employing a spectroelectrochemical technique in which 40 ms pulses were detected. Our results indicate the potential of this device to advance the study of cell activity and complex organ systems.

articleTitle: Optically Powered CMOS-MEMS Integration for Optical Transmission of MRI Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present and discuss an integrated CMOSMEMS chip design with suspended Fabry Perot bridges towards transmission of MRI signals. The proposed chip is optically powered, and offers analog or digital MRI signals transmission via fiber optics, towards safe and parallelized operation.

articleTitle: Fabrication of a Soft Photothermal Microactuator Using Two-photon Polymerization and Vacuum Filling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A fabrication method of a soft photothermal microactuator using two-photon polymerization and vacuum filling is proposed. Proposed microactuator was fabricated through two processes: A two-photon polymerization (TPP) and a composite injection by a vacuum filling. First, a PDMS microcantilever with a microfluidic channel was printed by TPP. Second, a PDMS composite containing thermally expandable microspheres was filled in the microfluidic channel. To validate this method, a microactuator with dimensions of 1 mm × 130 µm × 100 µm was fabricated. We demonstrated the ability of the soft photothermal microactuator to produce displacement of approximately 50 µm by laser heating.

articleTitle: Inkjet printing of polymeric optical resonators for multi-gas sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Inkjet printing of polymer microdroplets combined with plasma etching is used to fabricate on-chip high-Q optical microresonators for gas sensing. Devices made of three different polymers (SU-8, polystyrene and polyhexamethylene biguanide) are characterized with carbon dioxide and using vapors of isopropyl alcohol and water.

articleTitle: Enhanced 2D Beam scanning: optical-Phase-array on piezo-cantilever
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This work reports the development of an enhanced 2D beam scanning by combining 200 mm silicon (Si) photonics and 200 mm Si MEMS technologies. It demonstrates the fusion of an active photonic beam-steering circuit within a piezoelectrically actuated micro-cantilever. Operating at a wavelength of 905 nm, the optical phased array (OPA) enables beam scanning up to 17° in one dimension. Simultaneously, the circuit's inclination, in a second dimension, can be independently adjusted over a range of up to 40° via the piezoelectric actuator. This paper will focus on the technological process that combines photonics and piezoelectric materials, as well as the possibility of tailoring the cantilever resonance frequencies via the dimensional parameters, to suit various target applications.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of low dynamic deformation electrostatic micromirrors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Dynamic deformation of micromirrors is critical for high-performance display applications. A dual gimbal-frame electrostatic micromirror design that can reduce dynamic deformation is proposed and fabricated. Experiments show that the spot quality reflected from the mirror surfaces can be improved by the fabricated micromirrors.

articleTitle: Degenerate Frequencies Create Sensing Patterns for Single-Pixel Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A set of orthogonal trigonometric sensing patterns is introduced for single pixel compressive imaging. The mathematical theory underlying these functions draws from the natural phenomena of vibration and degeneracy. When combined with non-trigonometric sparsifying bases, a non-coherent dictionary matrix can be constructed. This approach facilitates high-fidelity image reconstruction while ensuring efficient encoding and decoding in terms of compression ratio and reconstruction time. Additionally, we demonstrate that theoretically these sensing patterns are robust against both Gaussian noise with varying variance and Poisson noise.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Design of Multimode Interference Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this work we present an approach based on Artificial Neural Networks through Machine learning techniques for the design of Multimode Interference devices. In order to demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed approach, several power dividers based on the multimode interferometer have been designed at a wavelength of 1.55 µm.

articleTitle: Achieving structural coloring with low-index polymer meta-pixels by multipole-based design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Conventional structural coloring schemes rely heavily on high-index, nanoscale structures that are complex and costly to realize. We demonstrate a new, multipole-based design which enables facilely tunable structural coloring in microscale meta-pixels made of low-index, soft lithography-compatible polymers, and verify the design with experiments.

articleTitle: Development of Graphene Resonant Sensor with PIN Photodiode for On-Chip Mass Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A high-sensitivity graphene-based MEMS resonance mass sensor is being developed to realize environmental virus detection. To increase its sensitivity and portability, it is necessary to integrate it with a PIN photodiode to enable on-chip resonance measurements. This report describes the fabrication and evaluation of such an integrated device. Graphene excitation was performed by a modulated laser and polysilicon was used to protect the device from the excitation laser, while a higher wavelength laser was used to probe the graphene vibration. On-chip resonance measurement was successfully realized with a SNR of 10 dB, demonstrating the feasibility of on-chip mass measurement with the fabricated device.

articleTitle: Electrically Programable Tamm Plasmon for Broadband Optical Neuromorphic Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Inherent limitations of traditional computer architectures have catalyzed the development of brain-inspired hardware, with optical solutions increasingly favored for their energy efficiency, speed, and scalability. Accurately simulating the synaptic functions of neurons with optical components necessitates precise tuning of resonators to specific wavelengths for multiplexed operations within photonic integrated circuits (PICs), a process integral to enabling massively parallel signal processing. However, as integration density increases, the task becomes further complicated by the challenge of arranging resonators of varying wavelengths within the confined two-dimensional space of a waveguide. Here, we propose a broadband neuromorphic computing approach using free-space optics that simplifies wavelength selection through straightforward parameter adjustments, consequently facilitating superior spatial configurations in a three-dimensional layout. We have implemented selective optical resonators enhanced by Tamm plasmon structures, which produce strong resonance through precise impedance matching, even in non-sophisticated planar structures, by integrating with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS). By modulating the thickness of the Tamm plasmon structures, we easily modified the resonance frequency with high precision. Consequently, leveraging the memory characteristics and non-volatile properties of PEDOT:PSS, we achieved expected results in enhancing the computational capabilities and efficiency of our system with a broadband and multiplexed optical signals.

articleTitle: Ultrathin Microlens and Microprism Array Camera for Hemispherical Imaging and Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report an ultrathin microlens and microprism array camera for hemispherical imaging. The camera comprises microprism arrays (MPAs), inverted multi-focal microlens arrays (MLAs), light-blocking layer, spacers, and an image sensor. The camera shows a field-of-view (FOV) of 180 degrees with a total track length of 1.07 mm. This ultrathin camera presents a novel opportunity in autonomous driving, security and surveillance, and medical fields.

articleTitle: Nonlinear semiconductor metasurfaces: from entangled photon generation to Terahertz applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Semiconductor metasurfaces are an outstanding candidate for creating novel functionality based on nonlinear optical phenomena. In this talk, I will present recent results in quantum metasurfaces, and metasurfaces for detection and generation of terahertz radiation.

articleTitle: Implantable Integrated Optical Device for in-vivo Phototherapy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is known for its benefits in cancer treatment; however, its success is contingent on efficiently delivering light to activate a photosensitizer. Recent technological advancements have facilitated the remote illumination of tumors, yet these methods face significant challenges, such as insufficient tissue penetration and inadequate activation of the photosensitizer. In this paper, we introduce a wireless, battery-free, low-profile implantable patch designed for low-power telemetry with smartphones to overcome these constraints. The smartphone transmits the required power to activate an NFC chip and an integrated LED, which serve as an optimized light source. The device features a compact and flexible structure and can be implanted in the body, where it receives power externally. In vitro experiments indicate that the proposed device is capable of wireless activation from a distance of 1 cm between the implanted patch and the smartphone, providing a stable power output of 140 μW to the nearby tissue. The device's performance was validated through a series of in vivo experiments in terms of power harvesting and LED light delivery to the organs.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin TMDC Transport Layers for Perovskite Solar Cell Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We propose a single-junction perovskite solar cell design using an ultra-thin transition metal dichalcogenide-based transport layers. We optimized the device performance with respect to the absorber thickness, defect densities, and transport layer thicknesses (electron and hole transport layers). Our simulation results indicate an excellent device performance with a high power conversion efficiency of approximately 33.7% alongside excellent key parameter values for the open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>), short circuit current (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>), fill factor (FF), and quantum efficiency (QE). This work provides a guideline to design cost-effective, ecofriendly, and highly efficient perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: Optical Ring Resonators in Sputtered Aluminum Nitride on Insulator for Integrated Photonic MEMS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This study explores the utilization of sputtered aluminum nitride (AlN) thin film on insulator as a platform for integrated photonic MEMS. We experimentally demonstrate proof-of-concept photonic ring resonators with Q-factors up to 31000 at a resonance wavelength of 1.5795 μm.

articleTitle: Bimorph Thermal Microactuator Fabricated by Additive and Subtractive Femtosecond Laser Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This study presents an additive and subtractive fabrication method for a bimorph thermal microactuator using TPP 3D printing and femtosecond laser ablation. First, a microcantilever with a thickness of 30 µm was printed by TPP 3D printing. Second, femtosecond laser ablation was utilized to reduce the thickness to 15 µm, which facilitated the creation of a bimorph structure. The cantilever-shaped bimorph microactuator demonstrated stable cyclic actuation, achieving a tip displacement of 11.5 µm through laser heating.

articleTitle: Pupil Center Tracking with a Quadrant Photodetector Using Bright Pupil Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We introduce a quadrant photodetector (QPD)based pupil tracker that outperforms traditional camera systems in speed and cost-efficiency. This innovative, compact system offers sub-millimeter accuracy in real-time tracking, optimized through QPD size simulations relative to pupil dimensions, promising for mobile and point-of-care eye-tracking applications.

articleTitle: Ghost imaging through dynamic scattering media based on expectation estimation correction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We presented a robust expectation estimation correction scheme in ghost imaging (GI) through dynamic scattering media. This method can effectively correct dynamic scattering problems with low computational complexity. It offers an enhanced solution for nonlinear scattering problems in GI.

articleTitle: A Robust Electrothermal Micromirror Based on Photosensitive Polyimide (PSPI) - Al Bimorphs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this paper, a high-impact resistive lateral-shift-free (LSF) electrothermal micromirror is proposed. The new bimorphs of the micromirror are composed of photosensitive polyimide (PSPI) and Al. Compared with the traditional micromirror, the impact resistance has been improved about 30 times.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Clear View Improvement through MEMS Smart Glasses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Recent experimental results confirm the strong reduction of optical artefacts for improved clear view through smart glasses comprised of metallic MEMS micromirror arrays using unusual irregular and unstructured shaped geometries. Concept, technology, investigated array geometries, and experimental achievements are presented and explained.

articleTitle: Highly Nonlinear Behavior of UV-curable Photopolymer during Low-Pressure Nanoimprinting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Understanding the dynamics of photopolymers in nanoscale environment is critical to many soft-lithographic techniques. Here, we report a highly nonlinear behavior of photopolymer arising from low-pressure nanoimprinting process. As the nonlinearity can degrade the patterning accuracy, we established a theoretical model to combat it.

articleTitle: Investigation of Mode Coupling Effect on Emission Spectrum of Organic Emitter in Microcavity with Plasmonic Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) are crucial for high-color rendering displays. We investigate the control of emission spectra by integrating microcavities with distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs). FDTD simulations reveal spectral changes and improved light extraction. For simple metal microcavity structures, increasing Ag thickness narrows spectra and induces blue shifts. Combining DBRs with microcavities induces energy splitting due to the coupling of the microcavity mode with the Tamm plasmon mode generated at the Ag/DBR interface. Ag thickness optimization also enhances light extraction efficiency. Our findings underscore the potential of microcavity-DBR integration for precise spectral control and enhanced performance in OLEDs.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Multi-band Terahertz Anisotropic Metamaterial Absorber Composed of Square-Shaped Resonator Array Featuring Three Apertures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a multi-band graphene-based anisotropic metamaterial absorber composed of a square-shaped resonator array featuring three apertures in the terahertz (THz) region. The absorber has a maximum of four/two absorption bands in transverse magnetic (TM)/transverse electric (TE) modes. In TM mode: two of the absorption peaks reach 100% and two other ones reach 85%, with an average absorption of 92.5%. In TE mode: the absorption peaks reach 50% and 89%, with an average absorption of 69.5%. The absorber has a maximum linear dichroism (LD) of 90%. The proposed device can be utilized in the design of future multi-task terahertz systems.

articleTitle: A 300mm silicon nitride photonic platform for ultra low loss in the visible spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper presents state-of-the-art values for a 300mm silicon nitride photonic platform in terms of ultra-low propagation loss for the visible spectrum. Achieving values of 0.3dB/cm at 532nm, this platform exhibits the lowest losses reported to date. This was realized by using a statistical method for material optimization of the waveguide, coupled with the use of the most advanced patterning tools.This platform is designed specifically for processing on top of CMOS wafer and can be enhanced with various functionalities.

articleTitle: Design of focus-tunable freeform microlens printed on kirigami MEMS actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This study proposes the design of a focus-tunable freeform microlens printed on a MEMS actuator. The proposed freeform microlens, designed with its varying surface curvature along the azimuthal direction, can adjust its focal length through the tilt motion of the MEMS actuator. The designed freeform microlens was printed onto a glass substrate, and demonstrated focus tunability ranging from 0.31 mm to 3.72 mm.

articleTitle: A Double-Sided Electrothermal Micromirror Array With Drive Resistance Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Electrothermal MEMS micromirror arrays are low-voltage driven optical modulation devices with large out-of-plane displacement. There is a critical challenge to realize uniform control over individual micromirror units. This study presents a drive resistance compensation method for the electrothermal micromirror array to minimize cross-channel resistance discrepancies. Based on this scheme, a double-sided, highly reflective micromirror array is fabricated and characterized.

articleTitle: Modifying the Complex Refractive Index of Thin-Films for Nanooptical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present a method to generate 2D refractive index patterns in thin-films for nanooptical applications, like metasurfaces and plasmonics. The method is based on standard deposition, lithography and manipulation processes and can be applied to numerous material systems. Examples for modification of indium tin oxide and transition metal nitride layers are given.

articleTitle: Ring-shaped MEMS Shutter Arrays for Interference Microscopy: Designs, Fabrication, Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Four different hinge designs for a ring-shaped MEMS shutter array demonstrator are presented, discussed and fabricated via an identical process. The resulting ring shutters are characterised and compared with respect to total transmission and actuation voltage.

articleTitle: Portable Raman platform for SERS droplets microfludics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this work we present the engineering of a portable platform for sensing SERS signals in droplets microfluidics. This system comprised not only the read-out platform but also a design for the microfluidic devices optimized to enhanced the obtained SERS signals.

articleTitle: Ellipsoidal Microlens Array Camera with Offset Apertures for Large-angle Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present an ellipsoidal microlens array (MLA) camera using offset apertures (OAs) to achieve high-resolution imaging at large angles. OAs facilitate precise focusing within a specific range of incidence angles, and ellipsoidal MLAs further minimize optical aberrations induced by substantial off-axis distances. The fully packaged camera successfully demonstrated improved large-angle imaging capabilities. The experimental results show that OAs significantly enhance the tangential resolution of large-angle targets at a 45-degree orientation while ellipsoidal MLAs exhibit a tenfold increase in sagittal contrast compared to spherical MLAs. This compact platform offers a new direction for wide field-of-view imaging in industrial and healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization of SOI-based Mach-Zehnder modulators employing deep neural networks and a non-dominant genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We combine an artificial neural network model of an integrated Mach-Zehnder modulator with a multi-objective optimization algorithm to optimize the modulator’s parameters. The use of a multi-objective algorithm leads to a set of non-dominant optimized configurations with different values of figures of merit.

articleTitle: Low-Powered, Full-Color Reflective Display based on Electrochromic Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Dynamically tunable reflective display is attractive for their applicability, due to high energy efficiency and clear outdoor visibility. While many reflective displays have been demonstrated, its monochromic color and high operating voltage are remained challenges and restricted their use in diverse electronics. Here, we introduce the full-colored monopixel reflective display (FMRD), which is achieved through a dual cavity structure with active material and lossy medium. As an active layer, polyaniline (PANI) forms a resonant cavity capable of changing its optical properties within a voltage range of -0.2 V to 0.8 V. To obtain a clear reflective color, we enhance light-matter interaction through impedance- matching between lossy medium and active layer. By designing porosity of lossy material with glancing angle deposition, it can be obtained and exhibits a deep reflectance dip. Additionally, the device successfully achieves the generation of the full red-green-blue (RGB) colors within a single pixel. FMRD is maintained half a day without power supply and reactivated its vivid colors after 4 months because self-passivation layer prevents the germanium oxidation. The protonation-based redox reaction plays a crucial role in achieving a fast response, with a rising time of 34 ms and a falling time of 171 ms. The photonic resonator operates at only 0.42 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per cycle and demonstrates scalability by addressing 25 pixels in a 5×5 matrix, indicating its applicability for larger-scale metrics.

articleTitle: Ultracompact Inverse Designed 1x2 MMI Power Splitter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present an ultracompact (2μm x 2μm) inverse designed 1x2 multimode interference coupler with lateral output ports based on the Indium Phosphide Membrane on Silicon platform and we analyze its principal performance parameters in the S and C bands for the fabricated devices.

articleTitle: Transfer of a high temperature LPCVD-SiN photonic layer on wafers with thermal budget limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the transfer of a LPCVD-SiN photonic layer to another wafer. In most cases the layer is transferred to a receiver wafer that has a limitation in thermal budget. The LPCVD-SiN layer cannot be directly integrated on receiver substrates such as CMOS or glass because of high deposition temperature but it can be transferred from Si carrier by bonding. Here it is demonstrated for two types of wafers (CMOS and glass) with a state-of-the-art propagation loss value for a 200mm LPCVD-SiN platform of 2.8dB/cm at 450nm.

articleTitle: MEMS Rotary Transmissive Grating Enabling Ultra-compact Near-Infrared Laser Scanner
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This paper presents a near-infrared (NIR) laser scanner developed using a microelectromechanical system (MEMS). The scanner leverages the transmitted diffraction beam of an in-plane rotational grating, offering notable compactness advantages over conventional reflective grating scanners. Experiment results demonstrate that applying 5V DC voltage induces an in-plane rotation angle of 15.8° of the grating. Furthermore, we successfully show the optical scanning of the second-order diffraction of the transmissive grating when driven by AC voltage. The frequency response indicates that the scan angle reduces with increasing driving frequency due to the limited electrothermal modulation speed.

articleTitle: Programmable Plasmonic-Nanopixels for High- Density Chromatic Information Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Efficiently modulating light-matter interactions in visible wavelength range holds significant importance for various applications such as optical encryption, switching mechanisms, and structural color displays. In this study, we introduce a novel approach for achieving electrochromic nanopixels by combining polyaniline (PANI) with metal-coated Si nanowires (Si NWs). Our optical modulation technique enables operation within an expanded color spectrum at a remarkably low voltage level below 1V, thereby ensuring energy-efficient performance. The intrinsic optical properties transition of PANI from reduced (dielectric) to oxidized (lossy) form, resulting in significant changes in its complex refractive index. Oxidation of PANI induces the effective cancellation of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) while simultaneously leading to strong broadband absorption due to an increased extinction coefficient. The fabrication process is versatile and can be tailored to meet various optical information encryption needs, scalable up to 8-inch wafers. A unique chromatic modulation capability enables the data encryption while leveraging the angle dependency of the waveguide to amplify the information capacity to 10 bits per unit cell. To further enhance the data storage capacity, our proposed system can incorporate multiple resonant structures based on diverse nanowire domains with varying dimensions to enhance chromatic changes.

articleTitle: Optimization of Fabry-Perot Interferometer Performance Through Low Mirror Roughness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: The influence of mask deposition temperature for TMAH etching to increase the optical quality of vertically etched mirrors is investigated. Better finesse and Q factor were obtained with PECVD compared to thermal oxidation. Lowest surface roughness reached was 8.41 nm for a Float-Zone silicon sample.

articleTitle: Exploration of 3D-printed lenses in a confocal MEMS microscope concept
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present the use of affordable 3D-printed lenses as critical elements in a small-footprint confocal MEMS microscope concept. Their excitation and imaging performance will be compared to commercial standard glass lenses.

articleTitle: Effects of the Refractive Index Data Set on Silver-Graphene Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this work, a numerical analysis was carried out using the finite element method to study an absorber composed of dielectric, silver and graphene. To demonstrate the behavior of the model using different data sets for silver and graphene, the absorption and reflection spectra in the infrared have been investigated

articleTitle: Fiber-Coupled Absorption-based Quantum Sensing with Nitrogen Vacancy Ensembles in a Suspended Diamond Photonic Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Low photon extraction efficiency limits the optical spin readout fidelity in emerging quantum sensing technologies in diamond. Here, we propose and fabricate integrated diamond nanoprobes based on cavity-enhanced IR absorption of embedded Nitrogen Vacancy centers. The design allows for near-unity readout fidelity, enables high spatial resolution and massively parallel detection schemes.

articleTitle: Angular dependent propagation in tilted multilayered structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this work, the electromagnetic propagation properties of an asymmetric absorber with artificial anisotropy has been analyzed. The proposed structure is operating in the visible and near infrared range with a high rate of absorption difference dependent on the incident angle, polarization and operating wavelength.

articleTitle: Potential and limitations of retrofitting commercial microscopes with refractive adaptive optics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: The past decade has seen the emergence of several novel refractive wavefront modulator technologies based on either piezoelectric or electrostatic actuators, which are functionally equivalent to deformable mirrors but work in transmission. Therefore, they can be potentially integrated into advanced imaging instruments without relay optics, and/or with significantly alleviated alignment and stability issues. This opens new avenues for wider deployment of AO in life-science microscopy, ophthalmology and free-space optical communications. The Deformable Phase Plate (DPP) developed in our group is one such technology, distinguished by its exceptionally compact dimensions, capability of high-order correction, and scalability, rendering it particularly useful for upgrading existing instruments with AO capability. We have recently run a multitude of experiments in which we integrated the DPP to commercial and research-grade microscopy and ophthalmology instruments. In all these cases, the DPP was coupled with different sensorless wavefront estimation techniques to minimize hardware modifications. In this paper, we summarize the results of these experiments and provide a critical analysis of the potential and limitations of plug-and-play AO upgrades from an end-user perspective.

articleTitle: Foveated, multi-spectral imaging systems inspired by avian eyes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Avian eyes have evolved a deep central fovea, enabling them to efficiently refract incident light for magnified imaging and effortless motion tracking of target objects. This adaptation is crucial for detecting and tracking objects in dynamic environments. Additionally, avian eyes can perceive a broad spectrum of light, including visible and ultraviolet wavelengths, facilitating the differentiation of target objects from complex backgrounds. Despite advancements in artificial vision systems inspired by animal vision, the exceptional object detection and targeting capabilities of avian eyes, utilizing foveated and multi-spectral imaging, remain underexplored. In this study, we present an artificial vision system leveraging these unique features of avian vision. Our system incorporates an artificial fovea and vertically-stacked perovskite photodetector arrays, whose designs are optimized through theoretical simulations to demonstrate foveated and multi-spectral imaging. Our artificial vision system successfully identifies colored and mixed-color objects and detects remote objects through foveated imaging. Furthermore, we discuss its potential applications in unmanned aerial vehicles requiring detection, tracking, and recognition of distant targets in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Investigation on Bistable Closing Behaviors of Metallic MOEMS Micromirrors with Various Initial Opening Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Pull-in phenomena of MOEMS micromirror arrays play an important role in electrostatic actuation. Pull-in behaviors of micromirrors with various unbiased opening angles are simulated, analyzed, and compared to experiments.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of VO2 kirigami electrothermal MEMS actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A kirigami electrothermal MEMS actuator using the phase transition material VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has been proposed. This paper reports the fabrication process and mechanical characteristics of the actuator. The actuator was fabricated by MEMS processes with VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> annealing method. Through the environmental heating, the actuator exhibited the bi-directional actuation due to the thermal expansion and phase transition shrinkage of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, resulting in a net downward displacement of 219.5 µm.

articleTitle: Overcoming Pull-in Limitations of Optical MEMS Based Micromirror Arrays Using Structured Bottom Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We report on design improvements of electrostatically actuatable MEMS-micromirror arrays to partly overcome the pull-in limitations utilizing tailored bottom electrode patterns for improved daylight steering into buildings. Concept, design, technological fabrication and experimental characterization of micromirror arrays are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Micromirror Arrays for Light Steering Smart Window Applications: Achieving Larger Spans of Opening Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: MEMS-based micromirror arrays in smart window applications are reported for active daylight guiding inside buildings. Concepts, simulations, design, technological fabrication, and C-V (capacitance-voltage) characterizations of micromirrors to implement larger actuation angle spans for improved daylighting are presented.

articleTitle: Silicon Nitride Microring Resonator with Metamaterial Side Cladding for Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: A microring resonator comprised of silicon nitride with metamaterial side cladding is investigated. A device with improved sensitivity is achieved by including such metamaterial cladding to the conventional microring resonator. The refractive index sensing simulation predicts a sensitivity of about 350 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: PIN-PMN-PT electro-optic phase modulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We fabricated a PIN-PMN-PT slab waveguide and made an electro-optic phase modulator. We characterized the electro-optic coefficient to be r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">51</inf> = 80 pm/V. This finding demonstrates promising potential of PIN-PMN-PT for integrated electro-optic applications.

articleTitle: Negative tone resist for grey-scale electron beam lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We present an innovative method to create free-form photonics element at the nano-scale. Our technique is based on the use of grey-scale electron beam lithography. By carefully controlling the exposure dose we can create a controlled three dimensional pattern.

articleTitle: Electronic, Stability and Optical properties of Strained Germanene monolayers: A DFT analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: In this study, we have investigated the electronic, stability, and optical properties of strained Germanene monolayers using density functional theory (DFT). Germanene is a two-dimensional allotrope of germanium which has attracted significant attention due to its potential applications in nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, and spintronics. By applying strain to the Germanene monolayers, we explore how their electronic band structure, stability, and optical properties are influenced. Our DFT calculations reveal that strain modifies the electronic band structure, resulting in tunable bandgaps and carrier mobilities. We also investigate the structural stability of strained Germanene monolayers under various strain conditions such as 2 %, 3 %, and 5 % etc. Furthermore, we analyze the optical absorption spectra and identify the impact of strain on the optical properties, such as real and imaginary components of the dielectric tensors. Our findings provide valuable insights into the tunable electronic and optical properties of strained Germanene monolayers, which could facilitate the design and optimization of novel electronic and optoelectronic devices based on Germanene materials.

articleTitle: A PDMS Micropillar Waveguide-based Microfluidic Viscosity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Optical knife-edge method is adapted to micropillar-based microfluidic chips for viscosity measurements. A laser is coupled to pillars that function as waveguides, whose output is monitored by a photodiode. We show that a photodiode can replace a CMOS camera, offering cost and computational efficiency advantage.

articleTitle: Multi-Core Fiber Tip Optical Excitation/Collection of NV-diamond Quantum Magnetic Resonance Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We developed an optical on-axis excitation / off-axis fluorescence collection system utilizing direct 3D-printing of refractive elements on the end-face of a multi-core fiber. The fiber-tip optical element is designed to operate as a highly sensitive magnetic sensor based on the quantum state transitions of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. The reported optical refractive element is fabricated by direct laser writing and two-photon polymerization. Such a fiber tip mounted magnetic sensor opens a novel paradigm of localized MRI in miniaturized form factor, potentially applicable for biological/medical scenarios.

articleTitle: An Improved Power-efficiency Microshutter Array with Thermal Isolation for Lighting Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Electrothermally-actuated microshutters suffer from high power consumption. In this study, an electrothermal microshutter array with Polyimide filled thermal isolation trenches is proposed to improve actuation power efficiency. The microshutter array has an optical aperture of 20×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the power consumption is 9.1 mW/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Tunable Directional Couplers for High Contrast Optical Meshes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We describe the operation, design, and fabrication of MEMS-tunable silicon-photonics directional couplers, with potential for smaller footprint, less sensitivity to fabrication errors, and guarantees of the desired split ratio. Our experimental verification demonstrates full switching with less than 20 V actuation voltage.

articleTitle: Stopband Fano Resonance Terahertz Metamaterial via Conductive Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Metamaterials offer extraordinary properties with prominent applications in various areas such as sensing, imaging, spectroscopy, or telecommunication. Metamaterials efficiency is very important in its electromagnetic response and is associated with the radiative and ohmic losses. In the case of plasmonic metamaterials, the non-radiative losses can be reduced by using highly conductive metal. However, there is a limit, especially in THz and optical frequencies. Thus, radiative losses play a more significant role in controlling the efficiency of the metamaterial. Here, we use Fano resonance to enhance the efficiency of a cross-resonator THz metamaterial. We use numerical and experimental methods to develop the design. Our results show a significant enhancement in the Q-factor of the metamaterial.

articleTitle: Development of Optical MEMS Gyroscopes with Integrated Interferometer and VCSEL Readout
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Optical readout is a promising approach to improving the sensitivity of compact MEMS gyroscopes. We report efforts to integrate a compact VCSEL laser for readout of displacement induced by the Coriolis force. As a diagnostic, we have first designed and fabricated a 2-axis vibratory gyroscope with mirrors for laser interrogation and performed electrical and initial optical characterization of the device.

articleTitle: Monolithically 3D nano-printed MEMS lens scanner for rapid focus control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: We discuss the design, manufacturing, and characterization of a 3D nano-printed electromagnetic lens actuator. The device features ortho-planar linear-motion springs and is monolithically fabricated by two-photon polymerization. With a resonance frequency of 482 Hz, the actuator is resilient against environmental disturbances, and achieves a quasi-static displacement of ±36.25μm.

articleTitle: High-quality object reconstruction using correspondence imaging through dynamic scattering media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: Object reconstruction with high quality through dynamic scattering media is reported using correspondence imaging (CI) with varying thresholds. The proposed method is experimentally verified to realize high-quality object reconstruction through dynamic scattering media, which is promising for potential applications in various scattering media.

articleTitle: Polymer-functionalized on-chip Fabry-Perot interferometer for CO2 and CH4 sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: An on-chip silicon Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) is functionalized with three different polymers to investigate the response to CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Polyethylene co-vinyl acetate (PEVA) exhibits notable sensitivity to methane at –3.36 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> pm ppm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> whereas having no sensitivity to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Waveguide-coupled GeSn membranes for mid-infrared silicon photonics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: The performance of GeSn membranes coupled to SOI waveguides for integrated photodetectors operating in the mid-infrared is investigated. Devices based on evanescent and grating-assisted coupling show a responsivity up to 361 mA/W at a wavelength of 2330 nm and a bias of 1 V.

articleTitle: Raman Spectroscopy Detects Biochemical Signatures in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: This research highlights the significant potential of combining Raman spectroscopy with machine learning models to improve the detection of lung cancer by analyzing human blood plasma. A total of 36 human subjects are involved in this study, eighteen of which are in the healthy control group and eighteen diagnosed with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC). The results revealed that Raman spectra from blood plasma were crucial for identifying significant vibrational changes in proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, and other biomolecules. Additionally, the study emphasizes the vital role of feature selection and multivariate analysis methods in achieving superior classification performance. It also explored the effects of mutations common in non-small cell lung cancer on Raman spectral shifts, but pointed out that further validation and search in the clinical setting is needed. The conclusion is that all machine learning models provide credible results, which shows that Raman spectroscopy is an effective method for future in vitro diagnostics of lung cancer.

articleTitle: Towards all-Silicon Micro-Mirror Array for space applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Optical MEMS and Nanophotonics (OMN)
abstract: MOEMS devices are key devices for next generation optical instruments, including space missions for Earth and Universe Observation, devoted to object/wavelength selection and wavefront control. MIRA is a European development of Silicon-based micro-mirror arrays, exhibiting remarkable surface quality and actual ability to work at cryogenic temperatures (162K). The challenge of operation at cryogenic temperatures requires the device to be ideally monomaterial to minimize the stress-related deformation or failure. This paper focuses on a specific plasma-assisted direct bonding (no intermediate materials) on Si micropillars as a key step to achieve strong connection at low bonding temperature (<400<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C) in multi-layer MOEMS devices.
